content: In order to be able to prove in some SetLike generality that gradings on graded objects can be changed (see this PR), it appears that I need an additional type class to indicate that the canonical map .ofClass from a class S of submonoids of M to Submonoid M preserves suprema.
I created a corresponding minimal PR some time ago, but forgot to post it here.

Given {S M : Type*} [SetLike S M] [Monoid M] [SubmonoidClass S M], we have canonical maps
S → Submonoid M → Set M
The first is Submonoid.ofClass, the second and the composition are coe maps coming from the SetLike structures. Depending on S, these maps may or may not satisfy various properties with respect the lattice structures on Submonoid M and Set M. Mathlib so far includes the type class [IsConcreteLE S M], which asserts that the composition S → Set M is order-preserving and order-reflecting. The type class defined here asserts that the first map, S → Submonoid M, preserves suprema.

In examples such as S = Subgroup M, S = Submodule R M, much more is true – in these cases, S is a complete sublattice of Submonoid M. But there are also examples where only the weaker property defined here holds, e.g. S = OpenSubgroup M for a topological group M.

The title appears to have been cut off (there's a length limit). What is the property you're talking about? Is it related to #mathlib4 > Abstracting the substructure lattice construction and #mathlib4 > More `IsConcrete` classes for `SetLike`?

Sorry for the cut-off title (now reworded). The property I'm talking about is that the map Submonoid.S : S → Submonoid M preserves suprema. Yes, it's very much related to the discussions you mention. These are long discussions, but my first impression is that the property I'm trying to capture here just adds another level of complication on top, since I am asking for an abstract supremum to agree with the supremum in Submonoid M rather than with the (different) supremum in Set M.
I don't think the right concept here is the .ofClass map. I think you should state that whatever concrete forgetful map preserves suprema.
Sorry, but I don't understand. ofClass (sSup s) = sSup (ofClass '' s) is precisely the property I want. What other map should I use instead if this is the property I want to capture?
The actual forgetful map of the concrete type you're using. I think making use of .ofClass will lead to all sorts of mess.

So what I’m actually after is a formalization and generalization of the fact that I can view an ℕ-graded monoid/group/module/algebra as a ℤ-graded monoid/group/module/algebra (with all components in negative degrees zero), or as ℤ/2-graded monoid/group/module/algebra (by “collapsing” all even degrees into one summand and odd degrees into the other). I had typed this out separately for monoids, groups, modules and algebras, but then was advised to develop this in greater generality using the SetLike abstraction. Unfortunately, however, in that generality this change of grading does not seem to work – the “collapsing” above really means taking a supremum, and that needs to be reasonably well-behaved in order for this construction to make sense.
So are you now advising me to forget about the SetLike abstraction altogether?

The construction itself can be stated within the existing SetLike framework:

variable {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
variable {ι₁ ι₂ : Type u} [DecidableEq ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₂]
variable (f : ι₁ → ι₂)
variable {σ : Type*} [SetLike σ M] [CompleteLattice σ]
variable (ℳ : ι₁ → σ)

def DirectSum.Decomposition.map : ι₂ → σ
  := fun j ↦ iSup (fun i : { i : ι₁ // f i = j} ↦ ℳ i)

(Think of f : ι₁ → ι₂ as the map ℕ→ℤ or the map ℤ → ℤ/2.)
But showing that this is actually a new direct sum decomposition requires some additional assumption.

Right I see
Possibly this can use SubmonoidClass.ofClass, by analogy with SetLike.coe
The issue is that use of .ofClass has led to big issues in the past that have needed to be refactored out - see the thread #mathlib4 > Mathlib's morphism hierarchy
The discussion you reference is specifically about FooHomClasses, not about FooClasses. Is there are parallel discussion/specification regarding FooClasses somewhere?

Artie Khovanov said:

Possibly this can use SubmonoidClass.ofClass

Do you mean “possibly this is actually fine as it is”, or do you mean “possibly you should switch from Submonoid.ofClass to SubmonoidClass.ofClass (which doesn't (yet?) exist)?

I meant Submonoid.ofClass - so possibly fine as it is - apologies for the confusion
The same considerations apply to definitions for substructures and morphisms - using .ofClass in a definition is considered an anti-pattern for both due to the coercion hell it produces
Great. Thanks for the clarification on both counts!
